Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Remittance files for Mar 10 sweep (two banks) — ACME

Hi Olga,

Attaching two remittance extracts from our payment provider for the March 10 collection run. Payments came through two different banks into the pooled virtual account and the remitter reference is inconsistent across lanes. Files attached:
- remittance_export_bankA_20270310.csv (CSV)
- remittance_export_bankB_20270310.csv (CSV)

We've flagged three lines where the parser didn't map invoice numbers cleanly and VAT appears to be split across items. Can you confirm how Redwood wants to handle:
1) Split payments that cover multiple invoices with VAT at different rates
2) Payments where the remitter reference is a transaction id (no invoice number)

We're on a tight close window for Acme's month end — any quick guidance appreciated.

Thanks,
Sven Holm
Head of AP Operations
Acme Solutions

Attachments: remittance_export_bankA_20270310.csv (CSV), remittance_export_bankB_20270310.csv (CSV)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sven Holm <sven.holm@acmesa.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Remittance files for Mar 10 sweep (two banks) — ACME

Hi Sven — thanks for the files. I pulled both CSVs through the parser and saw the three problem rows you mentioned.

Quick answers up front:
- For split payments that clearly reference multiple invoice numbers in the remitter text, our parser will allocate by invoice reference first, then pro-rate VAT by line amount when invoices have mixed VAT rates unless you instruct otherwise.
- For payments with only a transaction id (no invoice number), we try matching by amount and date window; if multiple candidate invoices exist we route to a suspense bucket and attach the payment trace for manual allocation.

Can you send the bank trace file for the pooled virtual account payment id "VP-20270310-4498" (there's one trace missing in the export). If you can provide remitter full name and the originating bank BIC for that payment it will speed resolution.

We can try a one-off rule: map transaction id VP-20270310-4498 to invoice #ACM-2349 and then re-run the parser. Marcus / Laura — if we accept that override, can we also capture the VAT split explicitly and post the remainder to a suspense GL code until confirmed?

Thanks,
Olga

Olga Petrov
Revenue Ops — Payments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: parser_sample_alignment.csv (CSV)

Hi Olga,

Thanks — attached is the bank trace for VP-20270310-4498 and the originating bank BIC (BKDNUS33) plus the remitter name (BrightByte Ltd). The trace shows an aggregate credit of EUR 22,930.00 that was split by our processor across two beneficiary lines.

Notes:
- We cannot retroactively add invoice numbers to the remitter field from our side — only the remitter reference (transaction id) is guaranteed.
- We have included an internal reference in the trace that matches your CSV row 127 (see bank_trace_20270310.pdf).

Let us know if the attached trace is sufficient. If you need a signed confirmation, we can provide a stamped bank letter (extra 24–48 hrs).

Thanks,
Finacore AP

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Remittance files for Mar 10 sweep (two banks) — ACME

Team — I ran a local dry-run of the parser with the suggested override mapping VP-20270310-4498 -> ACM-2349. Summary of findings attached (parser_sample_alignment.csv):

Key points:
- When we force-map the transaction id to ACM-2349, the parser pro-rates VAT across the two invoice lines and leaves a EUR 12.50 remainder due to rounding. That remainder should be posted to suspense (GL 9999) pending confirmation.
- There are two other unmatched small-value credits (EUR 1.35 and EUR 0.80) that likely relate to banking fees; suggest we treat anything < EUR 2 as fee variance and move to fee-variance clearing.
- Proposed rules to make permanent:
  1) If transaction id maps to exactly one invoice after manual override, apply pro-rata VAT and capture rounding remainder to suspense.
  2) If no invoice map, hold in suspense for 7 business days then automatically close to fee-variance if <= EUR 2.

If agreed, OLGA: please confirm and I'll schedule a targeted reconciliation job for Acme this afternoon.

Marcus
Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: parser_sample_alignment.csv (CSV)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sven Holm <sven.holm@acmesa.com>, Finacore AP <ap@finacore.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 17:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Remittance files for Mar 10 sweep (two banks) — ACME

Hi Sven / Finacore team,

Thanks for the quick trace. We agree to the following for the VP-20270310-4498 payment:

- Map VP-20270310-4498 -> Invoice ACM-2349 (manual override accepted).
- Pro-rate VAT across the invoice lines; any rounding remainder (EUR 12.50) will post to suspense (GL 9999) for Acme and we will reconcile when you provide the stamped bank letter or confirm remitter name/ID in writing.
- Small residual credits <= EUR 2 will be processed to fee-variance clearing unless you instruct otherwise.

Marcus will run the reconciliation job this afternoon and we will send a one-page allocation summary to Acme finance shortly. Can you confirm receipt and that the stamped bank letter will be available by EOD Thursday if required?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Manager, Billing & Collections
Redwood Inference
